enzyme_name: Hypophosphite/2-oxoglutarate dioxygenase (HtxA)
organism_context: Pseudomonas stutzeri WM88; htxA also horizontally transferred to Alcaligenes faecalis WM2072
rationale: HtxA is a mononuclear Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate dioxygenase purified from P. stutzeri WM88 whose only reported activity is oxidation of hypophosphite (phosphinate) to phosphite (phosphonate) coupled to 2-oxoglutarate decarboxylation; the downstream phosphite oxidation is a separate protein (PtxD). Note the MSDB equation puts H2O2 where the dioxygenase uses O2, and MSDB's phosphinate record carries formula O2P (mass 65 implies H2PO2-), so the two missing P-H hydrogens exactly cancel the O2-to-H2O2 substitution and the balance check passes spuriously.
direction_note: Oxidative decarboxylation of 2-oxoglutarate makes hypophosphite oxidation irreversible left-to-right; nothing reduces phosphite back to hypophosphite, so ModelSEED's reverse call cannot be enzymology.

enzyme_name: Glycopeptide aglycone sulfotransferase StaL
organism_context: Streptomyces toyocaensis NRRL 15009 (A47934 biosynthetic cluster)
rationale: StaL is a small single-domain cytosolic-type PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase; its crystal structures with PAP and with desulfo-A47934 show one sulfuryl-transfer active site and no second catalytic function, and it is the final tailoring step that converts desulfo-A47934 into A47934.
direction_note: PAPS is a high-energy sulfuryl donor and the transfer completes the mature antibiotic, so the written reverse (PAP + A47934 regenerating PAPS) is not a reaction StaL runs.

enzyme_name: Unidentified aminonitrile-hydrolysing nitrilase (EC 3.5.5.-)
rationale: The chemistry (R-CN + 2 H2O to R-COOH + NH3) is textbook nitrilase chemistry, but I could not find any named protein that hydrolyses 2-amino-2-phenylacetonitrile to L-phenylglycine; the entry has no EC, KEGG lists no hydrolytic reaction on L-phenylglycine (only R13515 / EC 2.3.1.331), and whether a single nitrilase or a nitrile-hydratase plus amidase pair is intended is undetermined. Calling this monofunctional would be a guess, so it stays unknown.
direction_note: Nitrile hydrolysis is irreversible in water; the written reverse (L-phenylglycine + NH3 to the aminonitrile + 2 H2O) has no enzymatic precedent, so the LLM direction is right whichever protein does it.

enzyme_name: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD, ACADM) acting on nonanoyl-CoA (C9)
organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation; chain length C9 falls in the MCAD (C4-C12) window
rationale: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenases are homotetrameric (MCAD/SCAD/LCAD) or homodimeric (VLCAD) flavoproteins with a single alpha,beta-dehydrogenation activity per chain; the specific family member is inferred from chain length, not confirmed for this Rhea entry. ACAD9's role in complex I assembly is non-catalytic moonlighting and does not count.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for the ETF/ETF-QO couple, which is why the written forward step has dG'o near +19 kJ/mol and ModelSEED calls it reverse; in vivo the electrons go to the quinone pool and the dehydrogenation is irreversible forward.

enzyme_name: Very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (VLCAD, ACADVL) acting on icosanoyl-CoA (C20)
organism_context: Inner mitochondrial membrane; C20 saturated acyl-CoA is a VLCAD/ACAD9 substrate
rationale: VLCAD is a membrane-bound homodimer carrying one acyl-CoA dehydrogenase active site per subunit. ACAD9, the closest paralogue, additionally serves as a mitochondrial complex I assembly factor, but that is a structural/chaperone role and is excluded as moonlighting, so the enzyme stays monofunctional.
direction_note: The irreversibility comes from ETF coupling, which the free FAD/FADH2 pair in this equation does not represent.

enzyme_name: Long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCAD, ACADL) / VLCAD acting on pentadecanoyl-CoA (C15)
organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of odd-chain fatty acids
rationale: A single alpha,beta-dehydrogenation activity on a homotetrameric (LCAD) or homodimeric (VLCAD) flavoprotein; family membership is certain from the FAD chemistry, the particular paralogue is inferred from the C15 chain length.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 replaces the ETF acceptor, which is what makes the written forward direction look thermodynamically uphill.

enzyme_name: Medium/long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on undecanoyl-CoA (C11)
organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of odd-chain fatty acids
rationale: Standard acyl-CoA dehydrogenase chemistry with one catalytic activity per subunit. Note the MSDB product record cpd34021 is named '(3E)-undec-2-enoyl-CoA', an internally contradictory locant string that is almost certainly a mangled (2E)-undec-2-enoyl-CoA; the chemistry is the normal 2-enoyl product.
direction_note: ETF coupling, absent from this equation, is what drives the dehydrogenation forward in vivo.

enzyme_name: Very-long-chain/long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on palmitoleoyl-CoA (16:1 delta-9)
organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of monounsaturated fatty acids
rationale: One dehydrogenation activity per polypeptide; the distal 9Z double bond is untouched and is later handled by the separate enoyl-CoA isomerase, so no second activity is involved here.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for ETF; the enzyme runs oxidation only.

enzyme_name: Long-chain/very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on heptadecanoyl-CoA (C17)
organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of odd-chain fatty acids
rationale: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase family, one catalytic activity per subunit; the particular paralogue is inferred from the C17 chain length rather than confirmed for this Rhea entry.
direction_note: The ETF acceptor that makes the step irreversible is replaced here by free FAD/FADH2.

enzyme_name: Very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on elaidoyl-CoA ((9E)-octadecenoyl-CoA)
organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of trans-18:1 fatty acid
rationale: VLCAD is a homodimeric flavoprotein with a single acyl-CoA dehydrogenase site; the trans-9 double bond of the substrate is a spectator in this step.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 in place of ETF is what inverts the apparent thermodynamic direction.

enzyme_name: Very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (VLCAD, ACADVL) acting on oleoyl-CoA
organism_context: Human/mammalian mitochondrial beta-oxidation; oleoyl-CoA is a canonical VLCAD substrate
rationale: VLCAD carries one alpha,beta-dehydrogenation activity per subunit; its regulation by SIRT3/SIRT5 and cardiolipin binding are not catalytic activities.
direction_note: ETF coupling, abstracted away here as free FADH2, is what makes the oxidation irreversible in vivo.

enzyme_name: Very-long-chain/long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on linoleoyl-CoA (18:2)
organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acids
rationale: Single dehydrogenation activity per chain; the auxiliary enzymes needed for the 9Z/12Z bonds (enoyl-CoA isomerase, 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase) are separate proteins and are not part of this step.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for the ETF couple that drives the reaction forward.

enzyme_name: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on docosahexaenoyl-CoA (22:6 n-3)
organism_context: Mammalian beta-oxidation of DHA; physiologically the first DHA oxidation is largely peroxisomal (ACOX1), but that enzyme uses O2/H2O2 rather than the FAD/FADH2 written here
rationale: The FAD/FADH2 stoichiometry identifies this as the dehydrogenase (EC 1.3.8.-) family rather than the acyl-CoA oxidase family, and those enzymes are monofunctional homodimers/homotetramers; which paralogue handles a C22:6 substrate is not established, hence low confidence.
direction_note: As with the rest of this block, the ETF (or O2, for the peroxisomal route) acceptor that enforces the forward direction is missing from the equation.

enzyme_name: Glycine betaine monooxygenase / demethylase GbcA-GbcB (Rieske-type oxygenase system)
organism_context: Chromohalobacter salexigens DSM 3043; homologous GbcAB systems in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and marine Rhodobacteraceae
rationale: The oxidative N-demethylation of glycine betaine to dimethylglycine plus formaldehyde is run by a two-component Rieske oxygenase: GbcA carries the single monooxygenase active site and GbcB is the separate reductase partner, so this is a multi-protein system, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: The real system consumes NAD(P)H and O2; the equation substitutes H2O/H2O2 for the reductant, yet the demethylation is still irreversible forward - betaine is regenerated from dimethylglycine only by SAM-dependent methyltransferases, never by the written reverse.

enzyme_name: Phospholipid N-methyltransferase (PEMT / yeast Opi3 / bacterial PmtA), second methylation PMME to PDME
organism_context: Mammalian PEMT performs all three methylations at one site; in yeast Cho2 does the first and Opi3 the second and third, so this step is Opi3/PEMT2-type
rationale: These are single-active-site SAM-dependent methyltransferases that iterate the same methyl-transfer chemistry on successive substrates; repeating one activity is not bifunctionality.
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible; the written reverse would be an SAH-dependent demethylation, which these enzymes do not catalyse.

enzyme_name: Exo-alpha-sialidase (ganglioside sialidase), GQ1b to GT1b
organism_context: Human plasma-membrane ganglioside sialidase NEU3 (also NEU4/NEU1 and microbial GH33 sialidases)
rationale: GH33 sialidases are single-domain glycoside hydrolases with one retaining/inverting active site that removes the terminal alpha-2,8-linked Neu5Ac; the specific human paralogue acting on GQ1b is inferred from NEU3's known ganglioside preference rather than confirmed for this Rhea entry.
direction_note: Hydrolysis releasing free Neu5Ac is irreversible; re-sialylation needs CMP-Neu5Ac and a sialyltransferase, so the written reverse is not a reaction any sialidase performs.

enzyme_name: Exo-alpha-sialidase (ganglioside sialidase), GT1b to GD1b
organism_context: Human plasma-membrane ganglioside sialidase NEU3 (also NEU4/NEU1 and microbial GH33 sialidases)
rationale: Same single-active-site GH33 exo-sialidase chemistry as the GQ1b step, removing the next alpha-2,8-linked Neu5Ac; no second catalytic activity is involved.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis with release of free sialic acid is irreversible; the reverse requires an activated CMP-Neu5Ac donor.

enzyme_name: Bacteriochlorophyllide d C-12(1) methyltransferase BchR
organism_context: Chlorobaculum tepidum and other green sulfur bacteria (chlorosome pigment homologue series)
rationale: This step converts the C-12 methyl into an ethyl group, the activity assigned to BchR, a radical-SAM methyltransferase; BchQ and BchR are separate single-activity proteins (BchQ methylates C-8(2), BchR C-12(1)).
direction_note: Radical-SAM C-methylation consumes SAM irreversibly; the homologue series only ever grows in the forward direction.

enzyme_name: Bacteriochlorophyllide d C-8(2) methyltransferase BchQ (ethyl to propyl)
organism_context: Chlorobaculum tepidum; BchQ is required for low-light adaptation via C-8(2) homologue formation
rationale: BchQ iteratively methylates the C-8(2) position (ethyl to propyl to isobutyl to neopentyl); repeating one radical-SAM methyl-transfer activity on successive homologues is not bifunctionality.
direction_note: SAM-dependent C-methylation is irreversible forward.

enzyme_name: Bacteriochlorophyllide d C-8(2) methyltransferase BchQ (propyl to isobutyl)
organism_context: Chlorobaculum tepidum; third round of C-8(2) methylation in the chlorosome pigment homologue series
rationale: Same BchQ active site, one more round of the same radical-SAM methylation; no second catalytic activity.
direction_note: SAM-dependent C-methylation is irreversible forward.

enzyme_name: Cytosolic catechol-estrogen sulfotransferase (SULT1A1 / SULT1E1), 2-hydroxyestradiol 3-O-sulfonation
organism_context: Human cytosolic SULTs; catecholestrogen sulfonation is a documented SULT1A1/SULT1E1 activity
rationale: Cytosolic SULTs are homodimeric single-domain PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases with one sulfuryl-transfer active site; which paralogue dominates for 2-hydroxyestradiol varies by tissue but none of them is bifunctional.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is a conjugation/detoxication step and runs forward; desulfation in vivo is done by separate sulfatases, not by reversal of this reaction.

enzyme_name: Benzylisoquinoline alkaloid N-methyltransferase (coclaurine N-methyltransferase type, EC 2.1.1.140), giving (R)-laudanosine
organism_context: Plant BIA pathways (Papaver, Coptis); (R)-enantiospecific BIA N-methylation is documented in Nelumbo nucifera
rationale: (R)-N-methyltetrahydropapaverine is (R)-laudanosine, and the only known enzymes performing BIA tertiary-amine N-methylation are the single-domain SAM-dependent CNMT/TNMT family, all monofunctional; the specific protein for the (R) substrate is inferred rather than confirmed.
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH N-methylation is irreversible; no SAH-dependent N-demethylase runs the written reverse.

enzyme_name: L-cystine C-S lyase (cystine beta-lyase; C-DES/Slr0077-type PLP enzyme); the same elimination on cystine is also run by cystathionine gamma-lyase
organism_context: Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 C-DES (sulfur mobilisation for Fe-S cluster assembly); analogous cystine-directed activity in mammalian CTH/CSE and plant C-S lyases
rationale: C-DES is a single PLP active site that performs a C-S beta-elimination on L-cystine, releasing cysteine persulfide (thiocysteine) and leaving the aminoacrylate; Slr0077 also shows cysteine desulfurase activity, but that is the same PLP chemistry on a different substrate at the same site, i.e. promiscuity rather than two fused catalytic domains. Note that the MetaCyc/Rhea entry writes only the elimination half-step: free 2-aminoacrylate (dehydroalanine) is really the enzyme-bound intermediate, and its hydration to pyruvate + NH3 is omitted.
direction_note: A PLP beta-elimination that discards an aminoacrylate is irreversible; the written reverse would be a spontaneous Michael addition of thiocysteine to dehydroalanine, not an enzyme-catalysed step.

enzyme_name: 2-phosphonomethylmalate synthase FrbC (homocitrate synthase homologue)
organism_context: Streptomyces rubellomurinus, FR-900098 (antimalarial phosphonate) biosynthesis
rationale: FrbC was cloned and characterised as the enzyme that condenses acetyl-CoA with 3-phosphonopyruvate to give 2-phosphonomethylmalate; like other citrate/homocitrate synthase-family TIM-barrel enzymes it has one aldol-condensation active site and no second activity.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of the acetyl-CoA thioester is what pays for the condensation, making the written forward direction irreversible for every member of this synthase family.

enzyme_name: Mn(II) oxidase MnxG, catalytic multicopper-oxidase subunit of the Mnx complex
organism_context: Bacillus sp. PL-12 / SG-1 spore Mn-oxidising complex (MnxE-MnxF-MnxG heteromultimer)
rationale: The active species is a multi-subunit complex (MnxE/MnxF accessory subunits plus the MnxG multicopper oxidase), which per the exclusion is not a bifunctional enzyme; MnxG performs two sequential one-electron oxidations, Mn(II)-to-Mn(III) and Mn(III)-to-Mn(IV), at one multicopper site, which is one iterated oxidase activity rather than two distinct ones.
direction_note: The written reverse would evolve O2 from water while reducing MnO2, which in biology happens only at the light-driven PSII Mn4CaO5 cluster; microbial Mn(IV) reduction uses unrelated respiratory cytochromes, so no enzyme runs this equation backwards.
